newsitem.title: USA: California keeps crown as top US exporting state.
newsitem.headline: California keeps crown as top US exporting state.

text.p: California repeated its position as the leading U.S. state for agricultural exports in fiscal 1996, the Agriculture Department said Friday.
Iowa again was second, followed by Illinois, Texas and Nebraska. The top 10 states accounted for 58 percent of the $59.9 billion in farm exports for the year.
Ag exports from California were valued at $7.27 billion.

USDA said the seven top states were unchanged from 1995. U.S. farm exports set a record last year, aided by high grain and oilseed prices. A record 21 states exported more than $1 billion in farm goods last year.
Exports this year were forecast for $56.5 billion. For the first half of the year, exports totaled $31 billion, two percent behind last year's pace.

California is a perennial leader in farm output, as well as exports, because of its size and position as a major grower of high-value products like cotton, rice, fruit and vegetables as well as grains and livestock.
